I and II are correct statements.

"Latent heat is released when a solid melts" is false, so III must be excluded.

The answer is I and II only.

text: Which of the following statements about latent heat is correct? I. Specific latent heat of fusion is the heat required to change unit mass of a solid to liquid at constant temperature II. Latent heat always causes a rise in temperature III. Specific latent heat depends on the shape of the substance
explanation:
Specific latent heat of fusion is the heat required to change unit mass of a solid to liquid at constant temperature — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "Specific latent heat depends on the shape of the substance" and "Latent heat always causes a rise in temperature" both misstate the physics.

So only I is correct.
